final_label: D1 after a rewarded common a2->S2 trial, late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the observed history favors S2 (belief < 0.5)

with_model_outputs.label: D1 after a rewarded a2 trial, late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the agent will repeat a2
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), almost exclusively when the reward input is 1 (99.9% of mass) and the previous choice was a2 (prev_action==1 holds 0.2% of mass; prev_action -1 is just the first trial in the window, where the choice is not visible). The agent then chooses a2 again (next GO choice a2 in >99.9% of activations; action at D1 is the agent own upcoming choice, which it can compute, not a random future outcome). It also depends strongly on episode time: zero activations before ep_trial ~55, then the rate rises from trial 60 to 99 (an episode-clock component). The policy logit at D1 is moderately negative (favours a2) and value is low/moderate. Magnitude is larger across a run of consecutive rewarded a2 trials (example windows climb 0.1 -> 1.0 over a streak) and in good=S2 / start_high episodes. Not active after unrewarded trials, after a1 choices, or early in the episode. Without the upcoming-choice term (observed variables only) F1 drops to 0.75 (precision 0.62), because of D1s after a rewarded a2 where the agent then switches to a1. Dev: P 0.75, R 0.95, F1 0.84, mass recall 0.996. The ep_trial threshold is approximate, since activation ramps up through trials 60-70.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: the predicate includes D1 steps after a RARE-rewarded a2 trial (a2 -> S1, rewarded). Adding (prev_common == 0) to the recorded predicate gives 5506 predicted test rows with 0 activations (precision 0.0). This is the model-based distinction the task is built around, and the label and explanation leave it out.

The same holds from the reached-state side. in_rew==1 & prev_state==2 & prev_action==1 (a rare-rewarded a1 trial that reached S2) gives precision 0.02 and mass recall 0.003. So the feature needs a2 + common + rewarded, not just 'rewarded a2' and not just 'rewarded at S2'.

Restricting to common previous transitions (prev_state in {-1, 2} & prev_common != 0) and keeping action==2 & ep_trial>=65 lifts test F1 from 0.825 to 0.884 (precision 0.73 -> 0.83, recall unchanged at 0.948, mass recall 0.995).
The observed-only version improves too: test F1 0.733 -> 0.795 when common-only is used in place of prev_action != 1.

prev_action == -1 (the window's first trial, where the previous choice is hidden) holds about 22% of activation mass. With prev_action == 2 strictly, mass recall falls to 0.78. The explanation treats this as trivial, but it is a large share of the mass, and the claim that the previous choice was a2 cannot be checked for that share.
Claims that check out: D1 only (phase != D1 has 0 activations); requires in_rew == 1; a1-common-rewarded trials give 0 activations; the upcoming choice is almost always a2.

Streak effect confirmed: many remaining false positives are the first rewarded trial after an unrewarded one. Adding tv('reward',-2) != 0 raises precision to 0.886 but lowers recall (F1 0.869), so the streak dependence is graded.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after a COMMON-rewarded a2 trial (a2 -> S2, rewarded; never after rare a2 -> S1 rewards), late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the agent will repeat a2; grows over a rewarded streak

with_model_outputs.final_label: D1 after a COMMON-rewarded a2 trial (a2 -> S2, rewarded; never after rare a2 -> S1 rewards), late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the agent will repeat a2; grows over a rewarded streak

label: D1 after a rewarded common a2->S2 trial, late in the episode (trial >= ~65), when the observed history favors S2 (belief < 0.5)
explanation: Fires only at D1 and only when the reward input is on (99.9% of mass), only from episode trial ~65 onward. The previous trial reached S2 via a common transition (or is at the window start). Replacing the banned upcoming choice (action == 2) with the ideal-observer belief that S2 is the good state (belief < 0.5) gives the same dev F1 (0.884); thresholds from 0.4 to 0.6 work about equally well. Misses are mostly weak activations after a rare a2->S1 rewarded trial. False positives are often windows where the trial two back was unrewarded; requiring that it was rewarded raises precision (0.90) but lowers recall (0.84). Activation looks larger after runs of consecutive rewarded a2 trials (seen in top examples, not quantified).

issues: Core claims hold: D1-only, in_rew==1 carries 99.9% of mass, zero activity before ep_trial 65 (in_rew==1 & ep_trial<65: test recall 0.02, precision 0.005), silent after rewarded S1 late (prev_state==1: precision 0.0), threshold 65 is best (60: F1 0.83, 70: F1 0.84).

Explanation's miss claim is wrong: misses are NOT mostly after rare a2->S1 rewarded trials (that class has recall 0.007). Misses (2.8% of mass) are spread over belief>=0.5 (recall 0.027), unrewarded D1 (0.024) and rare transitions (0.007); none is a large systematic class.

Window-start D1 (prev_state == -1) branch has precision 0.77 and the explanation's 'trial two back unrewarded' FP pattern is real (that subset precision 0.52), but adding tv('reward',-2)!=0 lowers test F1 (0.858).
Model output barely helps: adding action==2 raises test F1 only 0.872 -> 0.877.
